title: Greystone Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Greystone Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered goals, timeline, environment details (VPC, data residency), deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), initial pilot scope (chat and embeddings), success metrics, security/compliance requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and next steps (send SOW, security docs, pilot plan + benchmark). Assigned action items for both teams.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
action_items: Jordan Patel: Send draft SOW and pricing sheet by 2026-09-04
Maya Chen: Share pilot benchmark template and suggested prompts by 2026-09-03

Marcus Lane: Share VPC diagram and proposed subnet ranges by 2026-09-06

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM); Sofia Ramirez (Head of ML, Greystone), Ethan Cole (VP Eng), Priya Nair (Head of Security), Marcus Lane (DevOps), Aisha Khan (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're really excited to get Greystone onboarded. quick introductions — I'm Jordan, AE, I'll run the commercial bit and help coordinate.
[00:10] Sofia: Hi Jordan, Sofia here — head of ML. Looking forward to this.
[00:14] Ethan: Ethan, VP Eng, we'll handle infra side.
[00:17] Priya: Priya, security. I'll be driving compliance questions.
[00:20] Marcus: Marcus, DevOps. I'll do the VPC and networking stuff.
[00:24] Maya: Maya Chen, solutions engineer. I'll own the technical onboarding and the pilot benchmarks.
[00:28] Luis: Luis Ortega, CSM, will run the weekly check-ins.

[01:05] Jordan: Agenda for today — scope, timeline, who does what, pilot goals, security requirements, and deliverables. Any additions?
[01:12] Aisha: Quick note — product wants default responses to be audited, so logging / retention is important.
[01:18] Jordan: Noted.

[02:05] Maya: To start on tech — do you know if you'll go hosted, dedicated or private? we usually recommend hosted for fastest time-to-value unless you have strict data residency or on-prem needs.
[02:18] Ethan: Our initial goal is hosted but we need VPC peering and to keep raw PHI in our systems — so likely a hybrid: hosted with private networking and optional dedicated later.
[02:30] Priya: Security perspective: we need SOC2 artifacts, encryption at rest with KMS integration, SSO (SAML) and audit logs kept for 1 year. Also we need the option for a private control plane down the line.
[02:45] Jordan: That's all standard for our enterprise tier. We support KMS/HSM integrations and SSO; retention config is available in the console, and audit logs export to your S3 or SIEM. We'll share the security pack link after the call.

[04:20] Maya: For the pilot we recommend two routes: a chat assistant for clinician triage and embeddings for document search. Keep the model family open but probably start with a 7B quantized variant to lower cost, then evaluate quality.
[04:40] Sofia: Yes we want to be conservative cost-wise but quality can't drop — accuracy on triage must be > 92% on our eval set.
[04:50] Maya: Understood. We'll set up eval harness and a prompt set. we'll measure latency p50/p95 and token cost.

[06:00] Marcus: On networking — we need VPC peering or private link? what's the usual?
[06:06] Maya: We support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink, both. For hosted customers we do a managed peering plus egress controls. Some transcription notes: sometimes network names get munged in auto text, e.g., V P C might come out VPC or VPC egeres, sorry.
[06:25] Marcus: ok, I'll send our VPC diagram. we have NAT gateways in two AZs. we want to avoid public egress for PHI.

[08:15] Priya: Regarding data residency, we need EU region data residency for certain accounts. we have offices in EU — do you have regional hosting?
[08:25] Jordan: Yes, we have hosted regions in NA and EU and we can confine data to eu-west-1/region. For private deployments we can do on-prem but that takes longer (typically 3-4 months setup).

[10:00] Ethan: Timeline — we're aiming for a production pilot in 6 weeks. is that realistic?
[10:10] Luis: For a hosted pilot with VPC peering and a small eval set, 4-6 weeks is doable. For dedicated capacity or private it'll add time.
[10:20] Maya: Concrete milestones: week 1 — access & sandbox; week 2 — integration and initial prompts; week 3 — run benchmarks and adjust; week 4-6 — pilot iteration and metrics review.

[12:30] Jordan: On pricing — we'll send a pilot pricing sheet with committed capacity options. Pilot can be usage-based to start, then move to reserved if you need steady throughput.
[12:40] Sofia: We'll want an estimate for p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k requests with the 7B quantized model.
[12:50] Maya: We'll include a sample benchmark with tokens per request and cost estimates; note those numbers vary by batch sizes and caching. we'll recommend settings to hit your latency SLOs.

[15:10] Priya: Security deep dive — can you support customer-managed keys?
[15:16] Jordan: Yes, we support KMS and customer-managed keys for encryption at rest; HSM integration is available for private deployments.
[15:25] Priya: SSO?
[15:27] Maya: SAML and OIDC supported, SCIM for provisioning. we can put you in a trial SSO config.

[18:00] Sofia: Model governance — how do we pin model versions and handle rollbacks?
[18:06] Maya: The console supports model pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback to variant models. We also provide eval hooks to tie quality regressions to rollouts.

[20:30] Ethan: Any integration with our monitoring stack? we use Datadog and Splunk.
[20:36] Luis: We export traces and metrics; we can push logs to your SIEM and send metric hooks to Datadog.

[23:10] Marcus: A quick note: we run EKS in the VPC and prefer minimal NAT egress. will that be an issue?
[23:20] Maya: Not typically; we can route through peering and configure egress for private endpoints. We'll send a guide for EKS networking gotchas.

[26:00] Jordan: Customer success plan — Luis will be your main contact for weekly check-ins, Maya SE for technical calls, Jordan for commercial and escalations.
[26:12] Luis: I'll set up the recurring calendar invite after the call. first check-in target: 2026-09-08.

[28:30] Sofia: For success metrics — we'll define a pass/fail for the pilot: 92% triage accuracy, p95 latency < 800ms, and average token cost below $0.15 per request. are those reasonable?
[28:45] Maya: They're reasonable targets for a quantized 7B if prompts are tuned and we use caching. We'll document how to measure tokens cost.

[32:00] Jordan: Anything on legal / procurement?
[32:06] Ethan: We need standard SOC2 language and a Data Processing Addendum; procurement will start after they see the SOW.
[32:18] Jordan: We'll include DPA language in the SOW and attach SOC2 reports.

[34:40] Priya: One more: audit logs — can you keep raw logs for a year and provide redaction tooling?
[34:50] Maya: We have retention policies and an audit export; redaction is manual right now but we can discuss a workflow — also we support prefix/KV caching so raw user data can be excluded from cache. some of our notes transcribe KV cache as KV cash; ignore that.

[37:00] Marcus: Network firewall rules — we'll need a list of IPs/ports.
[37:05] Jordan: We'll send an allowlist and an install guide for peering.

[40:00] Aisha: On the product side, can we get an initial set of UI hooks for reporting incorrect triage outcomes?
[40:08] Maya: Yes, we have webhooks and a callback for feedback flows. We'll prototype a callback example.

[42:30] Sofia: For the benchmark harness — we have an internal eval set of 2k examples. is that enough?
[42:38] Maya: That's a good start. we'll run a baseline and suggest additional edge cases.

[45:00] Jordan: Recap and next steps — we'll send SOW, security pack (SOC2 link), bench template, allowlist, and schedule sandbox access.
[45:12] Luis: Action items captured: SOW by 9/4, benchmarks by 9/3, VPC diagram from Greystone by 9/6, security artifacts by 9/2.

[47:00] Priya: Quick question — what's the support SLA for pilot incidents?
[47:05] Jordan: For pilot we'll provide enterprise support with 4-hour response for Sev1 and 24-hour for Sev2, escalation path included. For Dedicated we can contract a stricter SLA.

[50:30] Ethan: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[50:34] Maya: No blockers. We'll need the VPC diagram and a contact for SSO.

[52:10] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with all links.
[52:20] Sofia: Thanks — excited to get started.
[52:25] Ethan: Thanks all.
[52:30] (meeting ends)

References / shared artifacts (mentioned during call):
- Pilot benchmark template: https://redwood.ai/pilot-benchmarks (shared post-call)
- Security pack (SOC2 + DPA): https://redwood.ai/security-pack (link to be sent)
- Onboarding guide / VPC peering docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding

Notes about transcript quality: auto-generated transcript contained occasional misrecognitions (e.g., "KV cash" for "KV cache", "V P C" spacing), filler words, and some speaker label switches in the first 30s. This export has been lightly cleaned but retains speech artifacts intentionally.
